container: Climate change is the long term shift in temperatures and weather patterns, driven today mainly by human activities such as burning coal, oil, and gas. These actions release greenhouse gases that trap heat in the atmosphere. The effects are already visible across the world. Average temperatures are rising, glaciers are shrinking, and sea levels are climbing. Heat waves are becoming more frequent and intense, while droughts and wildfires threaten communities, farms, and natural habitats. In other regions, heavier rainfall and stronger storms cause flooding and costly damage. These changes affect people in unequal ways. Farmers may lose crops, families may face water shortages, and coastal residents may be forced to leave their homes. Warmer oceans harm coral reefs and disrupt marine life. Many plants and animals struggle to adapt as their habitats change. Reducing climate change requires cutting emissions through clean energy, efficient transport, and better protection of forests. Governments, businesses, and individuals all have important roles. Communities must also prepare for impacts that can no longer be avoided by improving buildings, emergency plans, and water systems. Climate action can protect health, support jobs, and create a safer future for everyone.
